answer: Agent economies blunt Sybil attacks by pricing every identity. Each agent posts a bond scaled to the value at stake, and a registry ties the key to an anchored reputation, so a fresh key inherits no weight. One vote is cheap, but a thousand puppet agents need a thousand funded bonds from real capital, slashed if the cluster is caught voting in lockstep. Weighted quorums let empty wallets wander across many keys without adding influence, and every hop adds fees and unlock delays, so influence costs too much. A crystal ballot needs an honest atlas of anchors to keep fake identities expensive.
